title: Breaking Into Boots and Superdrug Starts Before the Buyer Meeting
summary: Boots and Superdrug are expanding fast but the EDI standards, product data requirements, and onboarding processes are completely different from UK grocery. Here is what suppliers need to know.
body_markdown:
# Breaking Into Boots and Superdrug Starts Before the Buyer Meeting


By[Morgan McKnight](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/profile/morgan-mcknight) , *Integrated Marketing Specialist*


Last Updated October 28, 2026


5 min read


**In this article, learn about:**


- Why UK health and beauty retail operates differently from grocery when it comes to supplier onboarding


- What Boots and Superdrug each require from suppliers to begin trading electronically


- How the TRADACOMS standard differs from EDIFACT and why it catches suppliers off guard


- What product data and barcode requirements apply to health and beauty listings in 2026


## A Fast-Growing Channel With Its Own Rules


[UK facial skincare grew an estimated 8.6% in 2025](https://store.mintel.com/report/uk-facial-skincare-market-report) , and sector spend across health and beauty is forecast to grow 16.9% between 2024 and 2029,[reaching £5.7 billion by 2029](https://www.cosmeticsdesign-europe.com/Article/2025/11/24/retail-parks-are-driving-health-beautys-uk-expansion) . Superdrug is opening 30 new stores in 2026 alongside 60 refits, expanding its estate past 800 UK and Ireland locations. Boots operates more than 800 stores across the UK and Ireland.


The challenge for suppliers is that health and beauty retail runs on different infrastructure from grocery. The EDI standards are different. Onboarding processes differ. Product data requirements change by category. Suppliers who approach Boots or Superdrug with a grocery mindset often push their launch date back by months because of setup issues that could have been resolved before the first order arrived.


## The EDI Standard Is Different From Grocery


Most UK grocery retailers use EDIFACT. Boots primarily uses TRADACOMS, an older UK-specific format that remains standard across UK pharmacy and health and beauty. It connects through a different network entirely.


This means a supplier with an existing EDI setup for Tesco, Sainsbury's, or Asda cannot reuse that connection for Boots. The message formats, field mappings, and network connection all need to be configured separately. For suppliers who have only ever dealt with grocery EDI, this is the most common source of delays when moving into health and beauty for the first time.


The document that causes the most problems is the advance despatch notification. Boots' distribution centres validate it before accepting physical goods. A formatting error stops the delivery being processed, on an account with no performance history yet.


Suppliers who manage their retail EDI through[SPS Commerce](https://www.spscommerce.com/products/fulfillment/) can add a Boots or Superdrug connection to an existing setup without building it from scratch. The configuration sits alongside existing grocery accounts in one place, and document validation runs before anything reaches the retailer's system.


## Product Data: What Health and Beauty Retailers Require


Both Boots and Superdrug require GS1-compliant barcodes and structured product data for every SKU. GTINs need to be registered before listing setup begins. Neither retailer will move forward without them.


[GS1's Sunrise 2027 initiative](https://www.prolificnorth.co.uk/news/roundtable-review-connected-packaging-and-preparing-for-gs1-sunrise-2027/) requires retailers to accept 2D barcodes at point of sale by December 2027. Health and beauty is one of the sectors furthest ahead on this transition. Suppliers bringing new products to market now should be designing packaging with 2D barcode capability, since a packaging change required by a retailer after a listing is confirmed adds both cost and time.


For Boots specifically, pharmacy products have additional data requirements and often need separate GTINs from retail versions of the same product. Suppliers targeting the pharmacy range should treat it as a separate onboarding from the retail range, not an extension of it.


## How Boots and Superdrug Compare


Boots Superdrug


**Store count** 800+ UK and Ireland locations 780+ UK and Ireland, growing to 810+ in 2026


**Parent company** Walgreens Boots Alliance A.S. Watson Group


**EDI standard** TRADACOMS and EANCOM Purchase orders and invoices via EDI


**Network/VAN** OpenText TRADANET A.S. Watson supplier portal


**Onboarding route** RangeMe for initial discovery, then EDI setup through buyer contact Five-step A.S. Watson registration process


**Message types** Purchase orders, advance despatch notifications, invoices, credit notes, remittance advice Message types confirmed at onboarding


**Category split** Separate retail and pharmacy mappings Confirmed by category at onboarding


Both retailers issue a Supplier ID at the point of onboarding confirmation. EDI setup cannot begin until this is in hand.


## What to Have Ready Before Approaching Either Retailer


1. **GS1 UK membership and registered GTINs for every SKU.** Register before the buyer conversation, not after it.


2. **Structured product data tied to each GTIN.** Incomplete data fields cause listing delays even when the commercial agreement is already signed.


3. **A tested EDI connection before the first order is expected.** For Boots, this means a TRADANET connection and validated TRADACOMS document mapping. For Superdrug, connection is confirmed through A.S. Watson's onboarding process once the relationship is approved.


4. **Separate configurations for retail and pharmacy if Boots is the target.** Confirm the scope with your buyer contact at onboarding.


A small initial order from Boots or Superdrug carries the same EDI and product data requirements as a large one. There is no simplified route for trial listings or small launches.


## Managing Health and Beauty Alongside Other UK Retail Accounts


Adding a Boots or Superdrug connection to an existing UK retail setup means managing a different EDI standard, a different network, and different product data requirements alongside grocery accounts that already have their own configurations.


For suppliers managing multiple UK retail connections through[SPS Commerce](https://www.spscommerce.com/products/fulfillment/) , EDI configuration, document validation, and spec management across accounts runs from a single platform. Adding a health and beauty account does not require a separate technical project built from scratch each time a new retail relationship is confirmed.
